*Alright, let me think this through...*

I'm 52, been at this for 5 years now — started when my husband took the construction work in Handan and couldn't come back for the busy season. My older boy's also working in the city. My daughter-in-law helps some when she can, and my younger son pitches in on weekends, but mostly it's me out there. 12 mu — not big, but enough to feed us and put a little aside.

Everyone in the village does wheat-maize, so that's what I do. You can't just plant one crop on this land — you'd be leaving money sitting. The turnaround between wheat harvest in June and maize planting is the hardest stretch. I pay the combine driver to come through for wheat, then the same week I need to get maize in the ground. No time to till proper, so I do no-till maize planting — the extension guy said it's fine and my neighbor Old Wang has been doing it for years with good results.

**For wheat** — I plant in mid-October usually, after the autumn rains cool things down. I buy Jimai 22 seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — it's what most of us use, resists the wheat rust pretty well. About 15 kg seed per mu, hand-broadcast because I don't have a drill. Before planting, I put down compound fertilizer, maybe 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15, that's my base. Then at jointing in early spring I topdress urea, about 15 kg/mu — I want to put more but urea isn't cheap and I'm watching the cash. That's about 16-17 kg N/mu total I think. The agricultural station man said I should be targeting 18 but I've never done that much and my yields have been okay.

Water — I pump from the village well. Winter watering once in December if it's been dry, then at jointing, then at heading. Three times for wheat, usually. More is better but the electricity for the pump adds up fast. For weeds I spray once in spring — just a cheap herbicide, 2,4-D type.

**For maize** — hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or something similar, my neighbor and I usually split a bag to save. I plant right after wheat comes off, around June 15. Same compound fertilizer at planting, then one topdress of urea at the big-trumpet stage, maybe 12 kg/mu. Maize doesn't need as much water if the summer rains come — last year I only irrigated once, in July when it was dry. I spray once for corn borer, that's enough.

My yield expectation? Last year wheat did about 420 kg/mu, maize about 480. I'm hoping for similar. Nothing crazy. If I get that I'll be satisfied.

The real worry every year is cash for fertilizer before planting — we don't have much saved by October. If my husband sends money home in time, I buy the better compound; if not, I buy the cheaper one.
